technology_name: Endemic Species Conservation with Ecological Niche Modelling (ENM): Habitat Suitability Mapping Tool
institution: KSCSTE- Malabar Botanical Garden & Institute for Plant Sciences (MBGIPS)
problem_solved: Identifying suitable habitats for the translocation of endemic plant species that have narrow distributions and poor natural dispersal mechanisms.
description: This study applies a Maxent-based Ecological Niche Modelling (ENM) framework to map habitat suitability for Crinum malabaricum, an endangered plant endemic to the Malabar Plains of the Western Ghats. By evaluating 21 bioclimatic and topographic variables, the model identifies key environmental predictors—specifically precipitation and mean temperature of the driest quarter. It successfully mapped 2,393 km² of highly suitable habitat (suitability index ≥ 0.85), which is significantly larger than the species' current extent of occurrence (283 km²), guiding the field selection of ten optimal translocation sites.
applications:
• Guiding target translocations and ecological restoration initiatives for forest departments and environmental conservation bodies

• Predictive habitat mapping and vulnerability analysis for endangered or narrowly distributed flora and fauna

• Integration into regional biodiversity action plans and environmental impact assessments (EIAs)

• Establishing scalable baseline modeling frameworks for climate change adaptation studies in fragile ecosystems
